approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs using only scores returned in the current session. It breeds a fresh field from a greedy population of sixty-four survivors, using score-weighted parent groups, connected-fragment crossover and short sampled runs of atom, bond and ring edits. Products pass canonical identity, duplicate and inherited sulfur checks. A count-fingerprint Gaussian process is refitted on the complete accepted archive before each announcement. It supplies means and a joint residual draw over the field, from which successive available maxima buy the announced batch. After three batches without a new incumbent, eligibility narrows to the forty highest means; the first improving batch restores the full field. The latest Parent removed an unexposed rejection-dependent edit floor and otherwise reproduced this loop exactly. Thus both fine mean preference and correlated residual exploration still operate inside the restricted set.
approach.novelty: Remove cross-candidate residual correlation only while the inherited stalled restriction is requested. Each candidate keeps its original predictive mean and its actual jittered marginal residual variance, and the original forty eligible identities remain eligible. Original independent normal coordinates multiplied by full Cholesky row norms replace the correlated residual transform in those announcements. The question is whether correlation still contributes after screening and fine mean preference have already concentrated purchases. This differs from the sibling that removed fine mean preference inside the mask, the sibling that shortened ordinary mutation walks, and the siblings that introduced regional or persistent-tree search. It also differs from the earlier correlation controls, which changed every allocation on mask-free Parents. The new scope isolates the retained correlation consumer without changing when the mask fires or how molecules are bred.

observed_bottleneck: The actual Parent n-cf8d309c06de uses correlated posterior residuals to decide purchases even after its stalled top-forty mean mask has concentrated eligibility. The unresolved behavior is whether this remaining cross-candidate dependence helps convert the screened field into paid progress. Its three actual summary.json/run.log pairs are successful: macro mean 0.607030316211131, population SD 0.030175277546149237; seed macros 0.649701282562401, 0.585233817344553 and 0.586155848726439. The available-seed aggregate records an exactly zero paired change against its own Parent, whose dormant mutation floor it removed. Read-only audits of all fifteen Parent logs and trajectories independently reproduce 435 announcements, 88 restricted and 347 unrestricted, zero fallbacks, 4,350 reconstructible original choices and 4,350 exact paid-identity joins. Restricted independent-marginal replay changes 83/88 purchase sets, displaces 186 actual purchased identities and changes 253 choices on the original per-pick available sets. All 88 restricted pools have nonzero fitted off-diagonal covariance. Two cells, deco_hop seeds 0 and 2, have no restriction and remain in the denominator. The records are policy/scratch/r0057-03-improve-L01/parent-audit-summary.json, its audit-seed-<Search seed>-<task>.json files and their explicitly listed underlying nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-<Search seed>/logs/<task>.log and trajectories/<task>.jsonl inputs; inputs-sha256.json preserves the exact files and hashes. The independent totals agree with policy/scratch/search_policy-ef020d29d984/anchor-correlation-audit.json. This audit reconstructs marginal scales from positive logged raw variances plus actual jitter; it does not claim historical Cholesky matrices or RNG-state receipts that were not logged. Direct conditional counterevidence remains material: n-8e00e5e9fc34 removed within-set location on this same Parent and lost 0.023092425745076712, so means must remain active for both consumers. The complete earlier m-000000000007 removals n-8df0bb3bbcfe and n-54adc6a641e8 lost 0.05054466462284635 and 0.018447481386582327 against their own mask-free Parents. Those results support correlation on those compositions, but neither isolates its restricted-only consumer here. Replay establishes an exposed test, not a purchased alternative outcome or expected gain.

hypothesis: For successful FingerprintPosterior.select calls on actual code Parent n-cf8d309c06de, retain the original fitted full posterior covariance C, actual successful jitter j, actual Cholesky factor L, original score_scale s, predictive mean vector mu and original normal array Z. Let d_i=sqrt(sum_j L_ij^2), using every entry of each full row. When and only when restrict_top_mean is not None, active values are A_ki=mu_i+s*Z_ki*d_i. Preserve original P_ki=mu_i+s*(Z@L.T)_ki as passive values. Every unrestricted call continues to use P directly. Thus restricted residual allocation covariance is s^2*diag(diag(L@L.T)), with zero off-diagonals and the exact original jittered diagonal; nonzero residual influence and both mean consumers remain. Eligibility stays the exact original stable mean-ranked set, and ascending pool-index first-maximum ties and per-pick availability updates remain. The hypothesis is that removing dependence changes strict and sequential restricted choices and reaches actual purchased feedback while preserving those retained quantities. This is a conditional component removal within m-000000000007; it does not change fitted covariance, remove residuals or remove eligibility. Prior exposed removal losses motivate a conservative prediction of a conditional endpoint loss, independently of whether this removal activates.

finding_summary.headline: Restricted residual correlation remained useful: its isolated removal changed purchases and lowered mean score by 0.00835
finding_summary.insights: This answers the narrow conditional question: residual dependence still contributes after the mean-based top-forty screen and fine mean preference have already concentrated the field. At the registered 0.002 descriptive scale, the isolated removal loss supports retaining that correlation consumer on this composition. It does not establish a uniform task benefit, generalization beyond this Search panel, or attainment of the separate Anchor performance target. Later unrestricted allocations inherited the changed feedback and cannot serve as untreated controls. The method also produced more nonempty typed scaffolds (1,764 versus 1,667), lower within-batch similarity even after excluding tiny fragments (0.4635 versus 0.4780), more parent-beating purchases (660 versus 634), and lower purchased-stream mean-squared prediction error, yet less total incumbent gain. These observations rule out treating extra graph diversity, more small improvements or lower global prediction error as sufficient evidence of better endpoint search. The molecular assessment still finds local elaboration of related ring-rich families and uneven retention of functional-group alternatives; the largest losing cell expands unusual heteroatom decoration while losing an amine-bearing alternative present in its better Parent series. That is an association within divergent adaptive histories, not the demonstrated cause of the loss. A graph proposal or search scheme that preserves distinct functional-group alternatives, or a ranking model that better identifies substantial incumbent gains, is the kind of method change that could address this limitation; neither is tested here. Matched Parent Candidate timings, historical factor/RNG receipts and trusted comparative task-safety measurements remain missing. No broader mechanism claim, approach-ending decision or sibling-effect subtraction follows.
finding_summary.results: The removal operated in 72 of 435 announcements and preserved the original predictive means, forty-candidate eligibility and marginal variances. It changed 218 of 720 restricted choices, changed 66 purchase sets and displaced 162 molecular identities; residual sampling still changed 586 restricted purchases relative to mean-only selection. Every one of the 4,350 purchases joined to actual feedback. Of the 218 changed purchases, 165 survived the batch and 57 later generated paid children; nine were censored by the final batch. The complete three-seed, five-task mean fell from 0.607030 to 0.598678, a paired loss of 0.008353. Seed macro changes were -0.006192, -0.019847 and +0.000981. Seven task/seed endpoints rose, five fell and three tied; the two unexposed cells reproduced their Parent trajectories. Full incumbent-gain mass fell from 5.978073 to 5.852783 despite improvement counts rising from 253 to 271. Late gain was almost unchanged, 1.022408 versus 1.020751 over 2,175 purchases. There was no execution failure and no registered falsifier triggered.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic and amine/carbonyl scaffolds persist, with frequent heteroatom halogenation and no defined stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: This assessment describes n-5e03d3ccd1b7 against the published code Parent n-cf8d309c06de using only the frozen Search seeds 0/1/2. Child evaluation and Parent pairing are both complete; no trajectory path or task comparison is missing. All 15 Child and 15 Parent trajectories were read: 300 accepted rows per cell, including ten initial records, giving 4350 optimizer-paid observations per node. These are accepted/evaluated molecules; unaccepted candidate fields are outside this chemistry denominator. Late means optimizer ordinals 146–290, trajectory evaluations 156–300, giving 2175 rows per node. Child paid molecules have median 28.0 heavy atoms, range 1–96; 4243/4350 contain rings and 4218/4350 aromatic atoms. This agrees with digest ring-closure rates 0.9701–0.9851 and aromatic-text rates 0.9632–0.9747. These rates describe molecules with a feature, not an atom fraction. The output spans familiar aromatic amides, aryl-linked amines and carbonyl-rich heterocycles, with many crowded or unusually decorated variants. Drug-likeness is only moderate structural resemblance; no synthesis, stability, pharmacology or safety was measured. Size tails <=5 heavy atoms are Child/Parent 103/91 full and 40/33 late; >50 heavy atoms are 43/44 full and 3/3 late. Empty Murcko scaffolds are 107/95 full and 42/36 late. Pooled nonempty typed/generic unique scaffolds are Child 1764/1037 versus Parent 1667/951 full; late 857/475 versus 774/414. These pooled unique counts are not sums of seed counts and do not establish synthesizable scaffold breadth. Within-batch sparse Morgan radius-2 count-Tanimoto means are Child/Parent 0.443107/0.459370 full (19575 pairs each), and 0.455538/0.477399 late (9600 pairs each). Excluding <=5-heavy-atom molecules gives 0.463511/0.477990 full (18667/18775 pairs) and 0.471797/0.491111 late (9250/9320 pairs). Similarity remains substantial after fragment exclusion. All paid molecules are represented with zero formal charge and no assigned tetrahedral stereochemistry; 2646 Child versus 2578 Parent molecules contain potential centres. Neutral notation does not establish physiological neutrality. N–halogen/O–halogen flags are 834/340 Child versus 888/162 Parent, with overlap allowed. The gaps below are conditional observations from these adaptive Search streams; they neither identify an activated algorithm component nor establish chemistry as a mediator. Evidence and exact definitions: policy/scratch/r0057-03-improve-L01-molecular/aggregate.json; policy/scratch/r0057-03-improve-L01-molecular/source-manifest.json; policy/scratch/r0057-03-improve-L01-molecular/citation-ledger.json. Child run-relative snapshots are byte-identical to the original trusted staging trajectories named in the manifest; published Parent files remain authoritative. Per-task text supplies each underlying trajectory and audit path. No held-out, Confirmation, human-selection rationale or external chemistry results were used.

per_task.generated_character: The main products are compact alkyl/methoxy-substituted fused aromatic heterocycles bearing aryl or pyridyl amides; seed 0 also develops a more condensed aza-ring system with a chlorinated aniline-type nitrogen. The seed 1 and seed 2 best molecules are indole-like aromatic carboxamides with N–F substitution. The seed-wise best molecules each have 25 heavy atoms, with three or four perceived rings. These are recognizable medicinal-chemistry-sized frameworks, but nitrogen halogenation makes synthetic plausibility questionable.  Paid Search panel: 870 Child and 870 Parent rows; Child heavy-atom range 1–41, median 25.0; 844 ring-bearing and 841 aromatic-bearing Child molecules. Child/Parent size tails <=5 heavy atoms 25/20, >50 heavy atoms 0/0. Parent best molecules retain related indole/aryl-amide chemistry; the Child broadens ring connectivity without establishing a different chemical class. Retaining both a sizeable aromatic region and a nitrogen/carbonyl region accompanies better scores. Extra ring elaboration does not by itself imply progress: Child/Parent endpoint changes have mixed signs despite many graph variants. Observed best scores by seed 0/1/2: Child 0.2112298000592183, 0.2253625707350009, 0.2421783688086956; published Parent 0.2228098910506594, 0.22127859918153825, 0.24240057874100313.

per_task.generated_character: All three seeds develop compact fluorinated, nitrogen-rich fused carbonyl heterocycles attached to partly unsaturated carbocyclic or nitrogen-containing side rings. Seed 0 leaders contain a cyclic secondary amine, an imino/carbonyl core and N–F bonds. Seed 1 instead favors a carbonyl-rich core with N–O–F/N–F decoration and a fluorocyclobutylmethyl side group, without the corresponding aliphatic amine ring. Seed 2 has fluoroalkyl substituents, an imino/carbonyl core and a small fused ring. The three best products contain 28, 28 and 25 heavy atoms and four perceived rings each. Child/Parent size tails <=5 heavy atoms 25/17, >50 heavy atoms 0/0. The Parent seed 0 and seed 1 leaders retain related cyclic amine-bearing side groups; the seed 2 equal endpoint belongs to different best molecules. liabilities: N–halogen and O–halogen flags occur in 333/870 and 207/870 Child paid molecules, versus 399/870 and 20/870 Parent molecules. The O–halogen increase is concentrated in seed 1, not a uniform change across the panel.

There are 345/870 small-ring-bearing Child molecules versus 270/870 Parent, and 603/870 Child molecules with potential tetrahedral stereocentres but no assigned tetrahedral stereochemistry. These features complicate a claim of ordinary synthetic or medicinal plausibility.

The Child still spends 25/870 paid evaluations on molecules with at most five heavy atoms. Its seed 1 final molecule is O, scoring 3.3466049979681925e-24; the final proposed molecule is not the best retained molecule.
missing_features: The seed 1 trajectory underrepresents the aliphatic amine side-ring chemistry present in the higher-scoring seed 0 and Parent seed 1 examples. The generator can produce that chemistry elsewhere, so this is uneven retention in a local series, not a universal inability or a task-specific structural instruction.

Stereochemically defined products and high-scoring analogues that preserve the compact carbonyl/imino and side-ring arrangement without N–F or O–F decoration are missing from the demonstrated leaders. No exact absent target motif can be identified from the scalar scores.

The Child seed 0 compact fluorinated amine-containing product (seed 0, evaluation 243, score 0.7118032602933165, 28 heavy atoms) is higher than its seed 1 O–F/carbonyl-rich leader (seed 1, evaluation 254, score 0.513036975067493, 28 heavy atoms). The large linked product (seed 0, evaluation 80, score 3.862281475007376e-18, 45 heavy atoms) scores 3.862281475007376e-18, and atomic F at seed 0 evaluation 110 scores 1.1043196211273875e-26. Parent seed 1's better endpoint accompanies a cyclic amine-containing product, while Child seed 1 has 188/290 O–halogen-bearing molecules versus Parent 7/290 and 25/290 amine-like-N matches versus Parent 91/290. transferable_gaps.evidence: In n-5e03d3ccd1b7, the complete paid Search panel contains 834/4350 N–halogen-bearing and 340/4350 O–halogen-bearing molecules; the paired n-cf8d309c06de panel contains 888/4350 and 162/4350. The cited leaders include N-fluoro amides and O–F-substituted heterocycles, while other leaders are conventional aryl/amine structures. These are overlapping structural flags, not observed reactivity or a component effect. Source: policy/scratch/r0057-03-improve-L01-molecular/aggregate.json and its source-manifest.json; all three frozen Search seeds, accepted proposals only.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve ordinary heteroatom bonding while elaborating otherwise recognizable molecular scaffolds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic graph generator could preserve chemically coherent heteroatom environments during edits and offer ordinary-bond alternatives around the same learned scaffolds. Any such change needs its own paired evaluation: high scores currently coexist with these flags, so blanket removal is not demonstrated to improve the objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The complete n-5e03d3ccd1b7 panel contains 2646/4350 molecules with a potential tetrahedral centre and zero with an assigned tetrahedral centre; paired n-cf8d309c06de has 2578/4350 and zero. Several cited high-scoring cyclic amine and bridged carbonyl products have such centres. Source: policy/scratch/r0057-03-improve-L01-molecular/aggregate.json, with per-cell descriptors and source hashes in its source manifest. This is a representation gap, not evidence that an unobserved stereoisomer scores better.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output can contain stereogenic ring and side-chain arrangements but does not express their tetrahedral configuration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: If stereochemical exploration is introduced, graph edits and identity handling would need to retain, create and compare configurations coherently using only current-session feedback. Defined stereochemistry should be treated as a chemical capability to test, not a promised score gain or an instruction to choose a benchmark-specific isomer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across the complete paired Search panels, n-5e03d3ccd1b7 emits 103/4350 molecules with <=5 heavy atoms and 43/4350 with >50, versus 91/4350 and 44/4350 for n-cf8d309c06de. Late counts are 40/2175 and 3/2175 versus 33/2175 and 3/2175. Cited tiny fragments and large linked products are much lower-scoring than connected intermediate-size relatives in the observed series. Source: policy/scratch/r0057-03-improve-L01-molecular/aggregate.json and its per-cell audits. The comparison does not establish a universal size optimum.
transferable_gaps.gap: Connected scaffold preservation remains unreliable at both destructive-fragment and oversized-recombination extremes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator could preserve a connected learned core during disruptive edits and make growth reversible, while retaining session-feedback-based alternatives outside that core. Evaluate both size tails and retained functional-group arrangements; do not infer a fixed molecular-size target or a universal ban from the pooled observations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One fully paired Search cell has 188/290 O–halogen-bearing Child products versus 7/290 Parent, and 25/290 amine-like-N matches versus 91/290 Parent; its cited best Child product lacks the aliphatic amine ring found in the better-scoring paired Parent leader. Other Child streams already produce amine-bearing leaders. The source is n-5e03d3ccd1b7 versus n-cf8d309c06de under the frozen three-seed panel; exact task, seed and original files are retained in policy/scratch/r0057-03-improve-L01-molecular/citation-ledger.json and source-manifest.json. The SMARTS match is not a pKa calculation, and this selected-stream association does not establish why the endpoint changed.
transferable_gaps.gap: Local series do not consistently retain useful amine-bearing side-ring alternatives when heteroatom decoration expands.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Retaining competing functional-group arrangements around a learned core could prevent a local decoration family from exhausting the available chemistry. Such exploration must be driven by current-session accepted outcomes and tested as a new generator capability; it cannot encode a named objective, prescribe one amine scaffold, or attribute this association to the allocation intervention.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
